title: Relaxation plus slow drift
claim: A two-parameter, causal prefix-conditioned forecast improves persistence and straight-line continuation on two reserved reactor runs. It loses to the flexible control and several other frozen candidates, so evidence supports useful short-horizon calibration rather than a superior or universal kinetic law.
scope: Complete reactor run. Diagnostic forecast after 300 min with fixed prefix calibration; no future conversion/selectivity predictors.
limitations: Public source-aware confirmation is now exposed.
Predictive success does not prove a causal mechanism, exhaustive novelty, or realized industrial impact.
Alternative valid equations are admissible under the same task.

title: Mechanistic or transfer falsification
claim: The second fitted relaxation time is not separately identified.
rationale: The two-timescale fit reaches the 20000-minute upper bound; its identifiable local drift limit is retained with a 1500-minute scope and no intermediate-species claim.
scope: The tested equations and current data only; no claim of universal impossibility.
